rule: Every entry is pinned to an exact live branch tip and is terminal only when current convergence preserves or strengthens the branch's valid behavior.

entries.rationale: PR #175 established physical-plan semantic invariance for source admission. Its SOURCE_ADMISSION_INVARIANCE.md is byte-identical on convergence, and every source-profile physical grain distinction, equivalence vector, semantic fingerprint field and deliberate negative control remains in current contracts/source-profile-model.json. The current contract further adds authority-manufactured stock-recipe tiers, explicit derived perfcache declarations, and a stricter authority-selected recursive seed manifest, so replaying the older branch would only remove later law.
evidence: docs/architecture/SOURCE_ADMISSION_INVARIANCE.md blob b1c055cea616a6fd51a13b6564c180cf96c3ea47 on branch and convergence

entries.rationale: PR #178 introduced the deterministic dependency-frontier planner and explicitly left common execution-provider/resource binding as the next slice. Current engine/include/laplace/detail/composition_frontier.hpp retains that planner and adds FrontierExecutionPlan plus BuildFrontierExecutionPlan, which plans every ready frontier through laplace_execution_plan_work under the execution-context resource grant. Current state therefore contains the branch behavior and the continuation it said was still missing.

PR #126 exposed the generated native machine-condition registry through PostgreSQL without semantic translation. The current integration has the same machine_exception_registry SQL type/function and the same descriptor-validation projection under integrations/postgresql/extension, with an additional deliberate capability-drift mutant. The old postgres/extension path is therefore a superseded package layout, not unique behavior.

PR #111 bound Unicode-native tokens, typed Glicko matchup/return-leg state, contextual importance and witnessed language realization into executable authority. Current contracts/trust-matchup-realization.json retains those laws and extends them with zero-attestation prompt/observation boundaries, exact-first structural and tier fallback, projection-collision safeguards, stronger user-standing return-leg distinctions and expanded deliberate-defect acceptance. Replaying the old requirement branch would lose later corrections.

This one-commit branch introduced exact installed Intel oneAPI provider selection, file verification, imported CMake targets, and custom-stack activation of LAPLACE_VERIFY_ONEAPI_INSTALLED_PROVIDER. Current main retains the installed-provider lock verifier and LaplaceOneApiProvider.cmake selection boundary, still enables it in the self-hosted custom-stack lane, and additionally consumes the verified provider in product package construction and provider-dependent tests. The older branch explicitly stopped before product-runtime activation, while current code carries the same verified selection forward into later package/runtime proof. Replaying the old patch would regress that stronger current provider lifecycle.
